panels.rationale: Single real clinical photograph of a left parietal scalp lesion in a 58-year-old man. The article title and in-text description explicitly identify a nevus sebaceus of Jadassohn with a yellow-to-tan verrucous papulated plaque and overlying alopecia; central pink and violaceous-to-blue nodules are also described and visible. Skin tone is not assessable because the scalp is largely covered by hair.

in_text_mentions: A 58-year-old male presented for an evolving mass on his left scalp. The mass was noted at birth and had been enlarging, changing color, and bleeding over the past 12 months. On exam, a 3.0 cm × 3.0 cm yellow-to-tan verrucous, papulated plaque with central, large pink, and violaceous-to-blue nodules was present on the left posterior parietal scalp with overlying alopecia (Figure 1).

in_text_mentions: A 46-year-old male presented to the dermatology clinic with a lesion on the scalp. The patient reported that this lesion had been present since he was a child and had not undergone any recent change. Physical examination revealed a 30 x 15-millimeter, linear, mamillated, tan-to-pink plaque consistent with the diagnosis of nevus sebaceus (Figure 1).
